html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. CLI: command-line interface; SLA: service level agreement; NDA: non-disclosure agreement

  • A time plan for 60 items in 120 minutes
  • How to read a scenario item, find the real question and eliminate distractors
  • Multiple-response tactics
  • Rules, policies and logistics on exam day, and what happens after

2Time Plan

Phase Time What to do
First pass about 80 min Answer what you know in about 80 seconds per item; mark doubtful items and move on
Second pass about 30 min Return to marked items; use elimination
Final check about 10 min Confirm every item is answered and every multiple-response item has the required number of selections
  • The guide describes no deduction for wrong answers, so answer every item; never leave one blank.
  • You must stay on camera (online) and may not use notes, phones or other material.
Exam tip

Mark a hard item and move on: it costs the time of two easy ones.

3Reading a Scenario Item

  1. Read the last sentence first ("What is the most effective first step?", "Which approach best...?") so you know what to look for.
  2. Read the scenario facts: logs, numbers and which agent behaved correctly. The cause is usually stated.
  3. Spot trigger words:
Word in the stem It points to...
"must", "always", "guarantee", "financial", "compliance" Programmatic enforcement (rule 1)
"first step", "most effective way to start" The proportionate, low-effort fix (rule 3)
"root cause", "logs show" The upstream cause (rule 2)
"blocking", "developers wait" Synchronous API (rule 8)
"overnight", "weekly", "nightly" Batch (rule 8)
"spread across the codebase" Glob-pattern path rules (Module 7)
"limited context budget" Structured, compact upstream output (Module 12)
"conflicting sources" Keep both with attribution (Module 14)
  1. Predict the answer before reading the options, then match.
Exam tip

The cause is usually stated in the stem (logs, numbers, which agent worked correctly).

4Eliminating Distractors

  • Cross out answers that rely on the model "remembering to" do something required.
  • Cross out heavy infrastructure (new classifier, routing layer, fine-tuning) when a simple fix has not been tried.
  • Cross out answers that hide information (generic errors, empty successes, dropping a conflicting value).
  • Cross out answers that give an agent more tools or more context than its role needs.
  • Cross out claims that a bigger context window or extended thinking fixes the problem (a bigger window does not fix attention quality; extended thinking does not replace independent review).
  • Between two valid answers, pick the one that is deterministic, specific, scoped and proportionate.

Multiple-response items

  • The stem says how many to select: choose exactly that number.
  • Judge each option on its own against the requirement; do not choose "pairs that sound alike".
  • If you can find only one clear answer, the second is usually the companion safeguard (for example a gate plus a handoff), not a repeat of the first.
Exam tip

When two answers would work, choose the deterministic, specific, scoped and proportionate one.

5Policies and Logistics

Topic What to know
Registration Through the Anthropic Partner Academy and Pearson VUE; pay at checkout; schedule online-proctored or at a test center
Reschedule or cancel Up to 24 hours before; later changes forfeit the fee
ID Valid government photo ID; the name must match the registration exactly
Accommodations Request and get approval from Pearson VUE before scheduling
Agreements You accept a confidentiality and non-disclosure agreement before the exam; never share or reproduce exam content
Retakes 14 / 30 / 90 days; max 4 attempts per rolling 12 months; fee each time
Result Pass/fail and scaled score, plus percent correct per domain
Validity and renewal 12 months; on-time renewal is a free, non-proctored assessment; if it lapses, retake the full exam
Appeals Within 14 days; the passing standard and item content are not appealable

[Verify live] Exam guides and exams are updated; the Architect – Foundations guide is version 1.0 (July 2026). Check the Partner Academy for a newer guide, the current fee and eligibility before you book. As of 8 November 2026.

6Final Review Checklist

  • I can state the ten decision rules without looking.
  • I can explain tool_use / end_turn and three loop anti-patterns.
  • I know why hooks beat prompts for hard rules, and what the handoff contains.
  • I can write a good tool description and a structured error.
  • I know CLAUDE.md levels, rules with paths, skills frontmatter, plan vs direct, -p CLI flags.
  • I know tool use + schema, nullable fields, retry limits, batch rules and SLA math.
  • I know case facts, scratchpads, escalation triggers, error context, stratified sampling, claim-source mapping.
  • I have built at least a small agent loop, a CLAUDE.md with a rule file and a schema-based extraction.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Time ~80 s per item; mark and return; check multiple-response counts
Method Read the question first · find the stated cause · predict · eliminate
Eliminate Prompt-only for hard rules · over-engineering · hidden errors · too many tools · "bigger window"
Pick Deterministic · specific · scoped · proportionate
Logistics Photo ID with exact name · 24-hour change rule · NDA · retakes 14/30/90 days · valid 12 months
